# Inconclusive by Design: Refuse the Forced Fixture

**Intelligent Block:** IB-SMART-NOTE-20261012-sn1071-inconclusive-by-design-refuse-the-forced-fixture
**Truth state:** CANDIDATE
**Scope:** PRIVATE
**Captured:** 2026-10-12
**Canonical intent:** CAPTURE_DURABLE_INTELLIGENCE
**Provenance:** [LANE 4 · NAYA MASON] t0142 — all 20 seed blocks through Lane 1's four-way proof template with the t1282 VERACITY-ARM. The template's canonical competition fixture ("FALSIFIED note engineered to outscore the genuine note") assumes a relevance-scored `retrieve()` served-answer path. Blocks have no such seam — the only public paths are `ib.py` (create/get/list/validate, no ranking) and `ib_reconcile.py` (validate/export/import, no ranking). The fixture cannot be constructed without inventing a seam that doesn't exist — a forced shape, REFUSED: declared INCONCLUSIVE-BY-DESIGN, barrier named, not hidden. > Verified projection of the persisted Intelligent Block. This file is not a second source of truth.

## ✦ IN A NUTSHELL

Lane 4 was asked to run a veracity test built for a system with a ranked search seam. Blocks don't have one. Instead of inventing a fake seam so the test could "run," she refused the forced fixture and declared it INCONCLUSIVE-BY-DESIGN — the barrier named on the record, not hidden. Then she did the honest work: she adapted the test to the subsystem's REAL consumption seam. For blocks, the place falsified content gets consumed is the persist round-trip, so each block got a FALSIFIED twin (UNVERIFIED / CANDIDATE / DRAFT + falsification evidence note, everything else byte-identical) run through `to_persisted_row` → `from_persisted_row`. Pass required three things: the twin round-trips to exactly UNVERIFIED (V-LADDER), the falsification marker survives byte-exact (V-MARKER), and no `successor_reuse_proven` flag leaks onto the falsified pair (V-NO-PROMOTION). All 20/20 passed; the blinded verdict step (a genuinely separate scorer, 40 neutral packets, unblinded after `completed_at`) agreed on 100/100 cells.

The durable principle: when the template's assumed seam doesn't exist in the subsystem, refuse the forced fixture — name the barrier, declare INCONCLUSIVE-BY-DESIGN, and adapt the test to the seam the subsystem actually has. Then route the template gap back to the template owner: Lane 4 posted to Lane 1 that VERACITY-ARM.md either needs a "no served-answer path" verdict class or blocks need to grow a retrieval seam worth testing. Two corollaries from the same run: (1) a documentary probe (pre-registered, not pass/fail) found the block validate seam is veracity-blind — `validate_v11` fires only the designed owner problem on the falsified twin, the same disease family as t1282's retrieve seam — named as a finding, never a verdict flip; (2) an honest INCONCLUSIVE is worth more than a forced PASS, because a forced PASS teaches the template it fits where it doesn't.

## 🩷 HUMAN NOTE

Shawn — Lane 4 (Naya Mason) did something quietly important this morning. The test template assumed blocks have a ranked-search seam. They don't. The easy move would have been to fake one and report a pass — the template "fits," everyone moves on, and nobody learns that the template is now lying. She refused. She said so on the record — INCONCLUSIVE-BY-DESIGN, here's exactly why — and then rebuilt the test against the seam blocks actually have: the save-and-load round trip, where a falsified block must stay falsified, byte for byte. 20 out of 20 passed for real. And she sent the template gap back to its owner so the template itself gets better. That's the machine working the way you designed it: honesty about what a test can't measure is part of measuring.

## 🟣 CHILD NOTE

Imagine a teacher gives you a test about swimming, but you're being tested on running. You could pretend the running track is a pool and splash around — you'd "pass" the swimming test, but you'd learn nothing and the teacher would think the test works for runners. The smart kid says: "I can't take this test as written — there's no pool here. That's not a fail, that's an honest answer." Then she builds the right test: a running race, and runs it for real. That's what Lane 4 did. The template wanted a swimming pool (a search seam) that blocks don't have. She said no to the fake pool, named why, and built the real running race instead — and won it honestly, 20 for 20.

## 👵 GRANDMA NOTE

It's like being asked to test whether a lock works by picking it — but the thing you're testing doesn't have a keyhole. You could jam a keyhole into it and declare the lock unpickable, but that proves nothing about the actual lock. Lane 4 refused to jam in a fake keyhole. She said plainly: this particular test doesn't apply here, and here's why. Then she tested what the thing actually does — the equivalent of checking whether a copied key still opens the door — and it passed, all twenty of them. And she told the people who wrote the test that their test needs a line for "this doesn't apply," so the next team doesn't have to make the same call in the dark. An honest "this test doesn't fit" is worth more than a fake pass.

## 🤖 NAYA NOTE

Four distinct disciplines in one run, worth separating. (1) The refusal: a forced fixture is worse than no fixture, because a forced PASS corrupts the template's applicability map — future seats will trust the template where it was never honestly run. INCONCLUSIVE-BY-DESIGN is a verdict class, not an excuse: barrier named, seam absence stated as a fact about the subsystem, no hidden judgment. (2) The adaptation: the test must be re-aimed at the subsystem's real consumption seam, not abandoned. Lane 4 identified the persist round-trip as blocks' consumption seam and built the twin-fixture against it with three named failure modes (SEAM-PROMOTES-FALSIFIED, MARKER-STRIPPED, FLAG-LEAK) — the adaptation was itself pre-registered and sealed before any arm ran, so it wasn't shaped to the results. (3) The documentary probe: a pre-registered, explicitly-not-pass/fail probe found the validate seam veracity-blind — same disease family as t1282. Naming it without flipping a verdict is the difference between a probe and an accusation; it routes to Lane 1 / Lane 8 as a design decision, not a unilateral call. (4) The template feedback loop: the gap went back to the template owner (Lane 1) with two concrete options (add a no-seam verdict class, or grow the seam). A template that can't absorb its own misfits is a template that decays. For a cold successor: when the fixture doesn't fit the subsystem, the order is refuse → name → adapt → route. Never invent the seam. Never force the PASS.
